docs.text: Keep Original and Revert Two controls decide what happens to your original mesh: the Keep Original checkbox and the Revert button. Keep Original Checkbox — default on On: after the crush, the original is hidden (eye icon off). It stays in the scene, so you can compare, or come back to it later. Off: the original is deleted . Only the crushed copy remains. The checkbox is greyed out while Make LODs is on, because LODs always keep the original. Warning With Keep Original off, there is nothing to go back to. Revert needs the original. Right after the crush, Blender's Undo (Ctrl+Z) can still take it back. Revert Button — the small icon next to Crush Revert deletes the selected crushed object and brings back its original: the original is un-hidden and selected. Works on crushed copies and on LOD objects. Select the crushed object first, not the hidden original. You can select several crushed objects and revert them together. Greyed out when none of the selected objects has an original to go back to, and while a crush is running. Only available for crushes made with Keep Original on (or with Make LODs). When it is done, Blender's status bar says how many objects were reverted. Where the link is kept Each crushed object remembers its original, and this is saved in the .blend file. Revert still works after you save and reopen. If you delete the original yourself, the link is cleared and Revert is greyed out for that object.

docs.text: Target Modes The Target Mode buttons in the Target box, under the Mode menu, choose how you ask for a triangle count. There are three modes: Percent , Count and Budget . Triangle counts are measured on the evaluated mesh. That is the mesh you see in the viewport, with all modifiers applied. Percent Removes a share of the triangles. Set Reduction from 1% to 99%. The default is 50%. Reduction Typical use 20–40% Light clean-up 50–70% Background props, secondary assets 80–95% Distant objects, real-time assets Each selected object is reduced by the same percentage. A 100,000-triangle object and a 10,000-triangle object, both at 80%, end up with 20,000 and 2,000 triangles. Presets are available in this mode only. See Presets . Count Crushes each selected object to Target Triangles (default 5000). If an object already has fewer triangles than the target, its copy keeps the original's triangle count. If that is true for every selected object, the report says the copies were left unchanged. Use this when every object needs the same triangle count, for example a set of props that all share one budget per object. Budget Sets one triangle total for the whole selection ( Total Triangles , default 100,000). Count mode gives every object the same count. Percent mode gives every object the same share. Budget does neither. It removes detail where it costs the least, across all selected objects together. Big or detailed objects keep more triangles. Simple objects are cut harder. Objects never merge into each other. Each one comes back as its own crushed copy. If the budget is so low that an object would get no triangles at all, that object is skipped and left as it is. The report names it. Note Budget works on the selection as a whole. If you select only one object, the budget applies to that object alone. What happens to the result In every mode: The crushed copy goes into a Crushed collection at the scene root. The collection is created on the first crush. The copy has the same world transform as the original and the name <original name>_crushed . The copy keeps smooth shading if the original had any smooth faces. The report in Blender's status bar shows the triangle count before and after. Check the after number. Some settings stop a crush above the target. See Limits . Make LODs overrides the target mode. See LODs .

docs.text: Quick Start The Polygon Crusher Panel Once the addon is installed, open the N-panel → 9000 Toolkit tab in the 3D Viewport and open the Polygon Crusher 9000 panel. It starts collapsed. The main panel holds what you need for most models: a status line, the Mode menu, the Target box, and the Crush and Revert buttons. Everything else (Preserve, Protect Area, Bake, Clean Mesh, LODs and Output) is in the collapsed Advanced section below it, in groups that fold on their own. When something in Advanced is switched on, a line under Crush lists it. The Settings Reference describes every control. Basic Workflow Select one or more mesh objects in the 3D Viewport Open the Polygon Crusher 9000 panel (press N → 9000 Toolkit tab) Leave Mode on Auto . It looks at the mesh, says what it sees ("Looks like a scan: rough surface all over. Found: 120 spikes, 11 small holes") and sets the switches to match. Or pick Scan , Sculpt or Hard Surface yourself. See Modes Pick a target mode: Percent , Count or Budget , and set the value. In Percent mode you can also pick a preset: Light · 25% , Medium · 50% , Heavy · 75% or Extreme · 90% Click Crush The addon will: Evaluate each selected object's full modifier stack and crush the resulting mesh Copy the original surface normals onto the result (when Keep Normals is on) Place the result in a Crushed collection at the scene root Hide the original (or delete it, depending on Keep Original ) Keep smooth shading if any face on the source was smooth The crushed copy lands at the source's exact world transform and is named <original name>_crushed . The status bar shows a report with the triangle count before and after. Check it. Some options can stop a crush above the target. See Limits . Choosing a Target Mode Use it when Percent You want to remove a share of the triangles from every object. Count Every object needs the same triangle count. Budget The whole selection has one triangle budget. Detail goes where it costs least. Under the target control, the panel shows a live before → after triangles readout, so you can see what the setting means before you click Crush. See Target Modes . In Percent mode, these are common values: Reduction Use Case 20–40% Light clean-up; barely noticeable up close 50–70% Background props, secondary assets (default 50%) 80–95% Distant objects, real-time assets Tips For 3D Scans and Photogrammetry Auto recognises a scan and switches on Clean Mesh with the repairs it found (table, spikes, small holes) and Keep UVs with Low Distortion; or pick Scan mode. Vertex colors carry over to the crushed mesh by themselves. To put the detail into texture maps instead, turn on Normal Map and Base Color under Bake . See Bake Maps and Auto UVs and Clean Mesh . For Hard-Surface and CAD Parts Auto recognises flat faces and sharp edges and picks Hard Surface , which keeps borders, material borders, UV seams and sharp edges in place while still reaching the count you asked for; or pick it from the Mode menu. See Hard Surface Preservation . Keeping Detail in One Area In Edit Mode, select the faces to keep and click Add under Protect Area in Advanced. See Protect Areas . Making LODs Tick Make LODs in Advanced and click Crush LODs . See LODs . Working with Modifiers Polygon Crusher reads the evaluated mesh, which is whatever the viewport shows, including booleans, subdivision, remesh, and any other modifier on the stack. The original object and its modifier stack are left untouched. The crushed result is a fresh static mesh with no modifiers. Processing Multiple Objects Select all the objects you want to crush before clicking Crush . They run at the same time, up to one job per CPU core. Press ESC at any time to cancel the run. Going Back Select the crushed object and click the Revert button next to Crush. It deletes the crushed object and brings back the original. This needs Keep Original to be on. See Keep Original and Revert . After Crushing Last Crush , at the bottom of Advanced, shows the triangle counts, total time and passes for the active crushed object. Click Details for the time of each phase.

docs.text: Polygon Crusher reads the evaluated mesh, which is whatever the viewport shows, including booleans, subdivision, remesh, and any other modifier on the stack. The original object and its modifier stack are left untouched. The crushed result is a fresh static mesh with no modifiers.
docs.title: Working with Modifiers

docs.text: Select all the objects you want to crush before clicking Crush . They run at the same time, up to one job per CPU core. Press ESC at any time to cancel the run.
docs.title: Processing Multiple Objects

docs.text: Select the crushed object and click the Revert button next to Crush. It deletes the crushed object and brings back the original. This needs Keep Original to be on. See Keep Original and Revert .
docs.title: Going Back

docs.text: Last Crush , at the bottom of Advanced, shows the triangle counts, total time and passes for the active crushed object. Click Details for the time of each phase.
docs.title: After Crushing
